verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes a right-angle JST orientation to preserve physical access when the power board is installed in its base.
The client adds the concrete PCB-layout condition that the installed board must not obstruct connection of the battery cable below it.
The client specifies adjacent battery and interboard JST placement with right-angle orientations, replacing the earlier generic orientation key.
The client adds concrete mechanical acceptance conditions requiring mounting-hole clearance and spacing between adjacent connectors.
The freelancer identifies a material PCB-layout conflict: the requested connectors and mounting holes cannot fit within the 40 mm board width.
The client resolves the fit conflict by relocating the battery connector to the back edge opposite USB-C; adjacency spacing consequently becomes obsolete.
The client-selected battery-connector relocation resolves the material layout ambiguity and permits connector-layout work to resume.
The client adds an enclosure-driven connector-access policy favoring top-edge cable connections and side placement for smaller connectors on vertically mounted boards.

value_updates.interboard_connector_status: eliminated under the single integrated-board architecture

verdicts.decision_note: The single-board architecture eliminates the interboard connector and its orientation requirement, but it does not re-scope the entire legacy power-board accessibility Requirement to integrated-board connector layout.
Through-hole connector assembly style belongs to REQ_CONNECTOR_ASSEMBLY_STYLE and does not change connector accessibility.
These battery and USB-C edge constraints govern the new integrated-board connector layout rather than the legacy power-board accessibility Requirement.

The client states that the former three-board cable-access constraints no longer apply under the single-board architecture, supporting removal of the obsolete legacy placement and clearance attributes.
